C or U: › [ C or U ] soft, wet ground, or an area of this

NONE: › used to tell someone to go away

example: Bog off and leave me alone.

NONE: › completely ordinary, without anything special added

example: My last car was just a bog-standard model.

NONE: › an insulting word for a person whose way of dressing, speaking, and behaving is thought to show their lack of education and low social class

C: › [ C ] in golf, the act of getting the ball into the hole in one shot (= hit) more than par (= the expected number) for that hole
（高爾夫球）超一擊，博蒂（高於標準桿一桿擊入一洞）

C usually singular: › [ C usually singular ] also bogie, bogy something that causes fear among a lot of people, often without reason
引發（常指無理由的）恐懼之物

C: › [ C ] UK informal US booger a piece of dried mucus from inside the nose

NONE: › (in golf) to score a bogey for a particular hole
（高爾夫球比賽中）在一洞打出超一擊，打出柏忌

example: the bogey of unemployment
失業的陰霾

他在第六洞打出超一擊，但在第七洞打出了博蒂。

NONE: › an imaginary evil person who harms children

example: Be good, or the bogeyman will come and get you!
聽話，不然妖怪就會來抓你！

I or T: › [ I or T ] to (cause something or someone to) have difficulty imagining or understanding something
（使）困惑；（使）難以想像；（使）無法理解
I: › [ I ] to be very surprised and uncertain about how to deal with something
（因吃驚而）猶豫不決，不知所措

example: My mind boggles at the amount of money they spend on food.

難以想像，對吧？
